To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the T wave is the result of a transient imbalance in the distribution of current between the two sides of the heart, (2) the amplitude of the T wave is a function of the magnitude of the transient imbalance, (3) this imbalance is a result of a transient difference in the magnitude of repolarization between the two sides, and (4) this transient difference in repolarization is a function of (a) the difference in magnitude of the action potential between the two sides

(1) the shape of the T wave is determined by the shape of the action potential of the cardiac muscle cell; (2) the T wave amplitude is determined by the action potential amplitude; (3) the T wave width is determined by the time constant of the action potential; and (4) the T wave is a manifestation of the recovery process of the cardiac muscle cells, not of the repolarization process.

the T-wave amplitude is a measure of the net repolarization current, the T-wave area a measure of the total charge transfer during repolarization, the T-wave vector a measure of repolarization current flow, the T-wave duration a measure of the duration of repolarization, and the T-wave slope a measure of the rate of repolarization.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects: (1) The origin of the T-wave; (2) The significance of the T-wave amplitude and its relation to ventricular repolarization and the QT interval; (3) The significance of changes in the morphology of the T-wave, and the relation of these to repolarization and QT interval.
the genesis of the T-wave of the electrocardio-gram.
the development of a new method of measuring the T wave of an electrocardiogram.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the T wave is the sum of the effects of a variety of mechanisms and that the individual features cannot always be assigned unambiguous significance.

the T wave is a manifestation of the repolarization of the ventricles, and that its amplitude and duration reflect, to a certain extent, the repolarization process in the right and left ventricle, respectively.
the T wave is a complex waveform which reflects the complex interplay of the electrical and mechanical events of repolarization and the subsequent contraction of the myocardium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the T wave is not only a reflection of the recovery process in the myocardium but is also a reflection of the repolarization process in the Purkinje system.
the T wave is not only the sum of the repolarizing action potential, but also a reflection of the preceding depolarization.
the T wave is a complex, multi-faceted, multi-dimensional phenomenon.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a number of the commonly accepted features of the T wave, such as its polarity, amplitude and shape, are not as significant as previously thought.
the T wave is a composite signal, which reflects the combined effect of the repolarization of all the cardiac myocytes, as well as the effects of the electrocardiovascular system on the signal.

, in addition to the conventional view of the T wave as a manifestation of repolarization, it is also a manifestation of the depolarization wave, which has not been sufficiently appreciated in the literature.
